models_evaluated: 30 general-purpose and medical LLMs (individual models not named in the text)

links.outcome: Whether strong diagnostic benchmark performance carries over to downstream care phases across 30 LLMs
links.effect: High diagnostic performance did not translate into improved downstream care; failure modes reversed across phases (staging errors 48.2%, omissions 33.4% in work-up and 30.4% in follow-up).
links.quote: Furthermore, NPC-RubricBench demonstrates that static diagnostic benchmarks are insufficient to ensure consistent clinical reliability over time, highlighting the importance of phase-adaptive safeguards in multistage medical AI.

links.outcome: Sensitivity of LLM decision quality, evidence faithfulness and safety adherence to query granularity
links.effect: Broad open-ended requests degraded Decision Quality across all 30 models; detailed checklist-like prompts raised Decision Quality but reduced Evidence Faithfulness and Safety Adherence.
links.quote: Moreover, varying query granularity exposes a critical specification trade-off: broad open-ended requests degrade Decision Quality across all 30 models, while more detailed, checklist-like prompts raise Decision Quality but reduce Evidence Faithfulness and Safety Adherence.

unlisted_practices: Phase-aware benchmarking of LLMs across longitudinal care pathways using decision-time evidence
Patient-specific atomic rubric criteria for evaluating LLM clinical reasoning

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM performance across longitudinal cancer care on a benchmark, explicitly testing the effect of prompt granularity (open-ended vs detailed checklist-style queries) on decision quality, evidence faithfulness, and safety adherence.
